questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: Compare the role of a nationalist rally with that of a constitutional conference in Nigeria’s movement towards independence. Explain how the two methods could reinforce one another.
questions.answer: A rally publicised demands and mobilised supporters. A conference let representatives debate and negotiate institutional changes. Visible public support could strengthen a negotiator’s case, while conference proposals gave organisers concrete aims to explain.
questions.explanation: The methods operate in different settings and can complement each other. Neither method by itself automatically transfers legal authority.

markingGuide.description: Explain the function of a rally.
Explain the function of a constitutional conference.
Explain a plausible link between the two.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: A timeline gives Nigeria’s federal constitutional reorganisation in 1954 and independence in 1960 the same label: end of British colonial rule. Explain why the label is misleading for the first event.
questions.answer: The 1954 changes reorganised government on a federal basis with regional institutions while colonial rule continued. The 1960 settlement brought independence. Constitutional reorganisation within a colony and the transfer of sovereign authority are different developments.
questions.explanation: Evaluate the label by identifying what changed in 1954 and what still remained to change in 1960.

markingGuide.description: Explain that colonial authority continued after that reorganisation.
Distinguish the significance of independence in 1960.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: Which activity most directly gave nationalist representatives a formal opportunity to debate the distribution of powers before independence?
questions.answer: Taking part in a constitutional conference.
questions.explanation: Conferences provided an institutional setting for representatives to discuss proposed constitutional arrangements.
options: Taking part in a constitutional conference.
Reporting a demonstration in a newspaper.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Explain how mobilisation and negotiation contributed to constitutional change.
questions.prompt: Which chronology best shows constitutional change before Nigeria’s independence?
questions.answer: Macpherson Constitution, federal constitutional reorganisation, independence.
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution dates to 1951, federal reorganisation to 1954, and independence to 1960.
options: Federal constitutional reorganisation, independence, Macpherson Constitution.
Independence, Macpherson Constitution, federal constitutional reorganisation.
Macpherson Constitution, federal constitutional reorganisation, independence.
Macpherson Constitution, independence, federal constitutional reorganisation.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: A student wants one source for the date specified in the independence legislation and another for the date of UN admission. Identify suitable sources and explain what each can establish.
questions.answer: The enacted Nigeria Independence Act identifies 1 October 1960 as the appointed day. A United Nations admission record establishes membership on 7 October 1960. Each source answers a different institutional question.
questions.explanation: Match the legal instrument to the independence settlement and the UN record to admission.

markingGuide.description: Identify the Act and its appointed day.
Identify a UN record and the admission date.
Explain why the records establish different events.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: A caption claims that the United Nations granted Nigeria independence on 7 October 1960. Rewrite the caption and explain what institutional roles the original wording confuses.
questions.answer: Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960 and was admitted to the United Nations on 7 October 1960. The independence settlement established Nigeria’s new status. UN admission was a separate decision about membership in an international organisation.
questions.explanation: Correct both the date and the action. Admission occurred after independence and did not confer it.

markingGuide.description: Give the correct independence event and date.
Give the correct UN event and date.
Explain the difference in institutional roles.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: Which date is the appointed day in the Nigeria Independence Act 1960?
questions.explanation: Section 1 identifies 1 October 1960 as the appointed day.

questions.subject: Nigerian History
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the 1960 independence settlement from admission to the United Nations.
questions.prompt: Which claim is directly supported by a United Nations General Assembly record admitting Nigeria to membership?
questions.answer: Nigeria became a member of the United Nations.
questions.explanation: An admission record establishes entry into the organisation. Claims about domestic constitutional arrangements require different evidence.
options: Nigeria adopted a republican constitution on the same day.
Nigeria’s regional legislatures were first created by the United Nations.
Britain chose the members of Nigeria’s delegation.
Nigeria became a member of the United Nations.
